verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 45% to $13.5B as Mounjaro and Zepbound volumes surged — and reported profit more than doubled to $4.4B, even after a $344M impairment charge tied to Vitrakvi.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot (tirzepatide) — U.S. revenue rose 25% to $2.6B and revenue outside the U.S. jumped to $0.9B as it entered new markets, partly offset by lower realized prices.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss shot sold in the U.S. — sales leapt from just $176M in its launch quarter a year ago as demand and supply both ramped.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else Lilly sells, including Verzenio at $1.6B and Jardiance at $1.2B — the Jardiance figure includes a one-time $300M collaboration benefit.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medicines — up 18%, driven by continued investments in the early and late-stage pipeline.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and running the company — up 26%, mainly promotional efforts supporting ongoing and future launches.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought in from other companies, expensed on the spot.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Charges primarily from an intangible asset impairment associated with Vitrakvi.

otherDetail: Net other expense of $110M — net interest expense of $180M, partly offset by $70M of net other income.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $4,806M (EPS $5.32). The release reports figures to one decimal place; they are rounded to whole millions here.
follow100Note: Mounjaro and Zepbound together supplied $40.17 of every $100 Lilly took in — two versions of the same drug, tirzepatide. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Two drugs drove the growth
takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($3.5B, +60%) and Zepbound ($1.9B, up from $176M in its launch quarter) together brought in $5.4B — 40% of all revenue. Overall volume rose 48%, partly offset by 4% lower realized prices.

takeaways.title: Margins widened again
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 1.3 points to 82.2% on a favorable product mix, partly offset by lower realized prices — so operating income more than doubled, to $5.1B.

takeaways.title: 2025 guidance issued
takeaways.text: Lilly guided 2025 revenue to $58.0–61.0B with reported EPS of $22.05–23.55, and said it would produce at least 1.6 times as many salable incretin doses in the first half of 2025 as a year earlier.

oneTimers: Asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges of $344M — primarily an intangible asset impairment associated with Vitrakvi. They cost $0.30 of the quarter's EPS on a non-GAAP comparison basis.
Acquired IPR&D charges of $189M ($0.19 of EPS), down from $623M a year ago, when the charges mainly related to Mablink Biosciences and a Beam Therapeutics transaction.

Jardiance revenue included a one-time benefit of $300M from an amendment to the Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration that adjusted who sells Jardiance in certain markets — that benefit sits inside 'All other medicines' revenue.
